title.narrative: São Gonçalo 2030: Strengthening the planning and management of the Municipality of São Gonçalo to build a more sustainable and safer city, that leaves no one and no territory behind

description.narrative:
This project aims to support the Municipal Government of São Gonçalo to reduce inequalities in the municipality based on the fulfilment of the 2030 Agenda in the city. In particular, the proposal focuses on improving the capacities and conditions of the Municipality Direct Administration in monitoring of urban conditions and trends at the local level and providing evidence-based information to build sustainable and integrated urban policies locally, complementing the objectives of the city's Strategic Plan, called Novos Rumos, and the five pillars that guide it: transparent and efficient public administration, safe city, well-cared city, healthy city and fair and inclusive city.
To achieve the proposed objective, the São Gonçalo municipality proposes a partnership with the United Nations Programme for Human Settlements (UN-Habitat) focused on strengthening technical capacities, improvement and standardization of monitoring systems and use of data, innovation in public management and community mobilization and participation.
The use of UN-Habitat methodologies and tools is planned as a starting point for the project. In the output of the urban observatory, the methodologies applied aim to support the local government to develop public policies based on evidence and timely information. To this end, an Indicators Framework and a Monitoring System will be elaborated built on the Global Urban Monitoring Framework (UMF) with the objective of providing inputs to produce periodical Thematic Notebooks that can support the elaboration of more effective policies in the municipality, including studies and research related to the themes of innovation, government transformation and safety, based on the 17 SDGs.
Based on the framework, the project will build an open data platform for enable the municipality to monitor the progress made from the implemented policies and their correlation with the SDGs. This will be an opportunity to foster and strengthen collaboration between Secretaries and promote cross-sectoral collaboration within government departments, aiming at improving government efficiency to conduct policies that have social, economic and environmental impact at the local level. This will also intend to support the municipality in realigning their budget to channel effective actions to better alleviate the socioeconomic and infrastructure municipal disparities in a sustainable and transformative manner.
This will be complemented with a capacity development output where UN-Habitat will work with the various departments involved in the project to use the data and information produced to follow up on municipal planning with an integrated approach to policies. The training programme will also include forums to discuss the thematic notebooks and in person or virtually exchanges with other Brazilian and Latin American municipalities with similar realities to that of São Gonçalo.
Another output will focus on building security diagnostics and action plans to inform and guide urban planning, development and management. UN-Habitat will work with the municipal government on a human rights-based approach to enhance the prevention policies of São Gonçalo through intersectoral data collection, safety diagnostics in prioritized territories, engagement of public servants, and action planning and investment preparations. The main results of the process will be the development of strategies for Urban Safety and Crime Prevention in São Gonçalo
Following the diagnosis, the project team and São Gonçalo municipality will design and implement a Planning and Design Lab for Sustainable Urban Development in São Gonçalo through immersion activities focused on one or two of the Municipal Strategic Plan axes. Using planning and design as tools for integrating the work across different sectors within the local administration, the urban lab will promote an integrated approach that combines spatial, legal, financial, social and environmental strategies to deliver concrete and improved policies.
Additionally, there will be an output to involve the local population, especially women, in building architectural designs for prioritized public spaces. The Public Space Designs workshops, which will happen using block-by-block or an adapted tool with physical models, will promote community participation in the decision-making process for the redesign of urban spaces and the adherence of the population to comply with the 2030 Agenda. The project will consider Her City orientations to apply a gender lens by evaluating and identifying the public spaces to be prioritized in a participatory process that place women and girls, people with disabilities, children, youth and older persons and persons in vulnerable situations in the centre of urban planning and design, taking as a principle that they plan and design with diversity and needs in mind different of that from the actors that usually lead and are heard.
